text:
maria: Quick question — we're trying to produce a single "user-facing latency" SLO from traces. Goal: 99th for the whole request but also break down into (queue, network, compute). Two big concerns: sampling + exporter retention biasing the percentiles, and how to compute the breakdown from spans reliably. Any recommended approach?
kevin: For breakdown, use span relationships. Root span = total. compute = span named model.infer (or longest child). network = http.client / net.* spans. queue = total - sum(known child durations). Simple math:
```
# pseudocode
total = duration(root)
compute = duration(span['model.infer'])
network = sum(duration(s) for s in spans if s.kind=='client' and s.name contains 'http')
queue = total - (compute + network)
```
that works if spans are present and clock skew is minimal.
oliver: main gotcha = sampling/retention. If we tail-sample slow traces that's fine, but head-based sampling + low retention means the tail percentiles will look better than reality. Two mitigations: 1) derive metrics from traces at ingest (histogram buckets) and write those to metrics store — compute SLO from the metric, not raw traces. 2) apply weighted sampling: annotate kept traces with sampling_rate so you can weight them when computing percentiles. Both have tradeoffs.
jess: For dashboards we usually compute percentiles in the metrics DB. Example SQL-ish query for the derived metric:
```
SELECT percentile(duration_ms, 99) FROM trace_latency_metric WHERE service='ui' AND route='/search' GROUP BY time(1m)
```
Then overlay retention/exporter lag as another line.
kevin: About weighting — if you keep 1/10 traces, assign weight 10 to each kept trace when computing quantiles. But quantile weighting is tricky; you can approximate with histogram buckets: multiply counts by 1/sample_rate. Proper tail quantiles still need enough samples.
maria: Okay — so two actionable items: (A) ensure we have a derived histogram metric at ingest for key ops, (B) tag/retain slow traces with a keep flag so we don't lose tails. Any advice on exporter configuration (OTLP/Jaeger) or retention alerts?
oliver: OTLP + collector tail-sampling for slow traces works. Configure collector to always keep traces where duration_ms > 1000 or where error==true. Also emit a retention metric: `traces.retained_ratio{env}` (kept / incoming) and exporter_lag gauge. Add alerts: if traces.retained_ratio drops >5% or exporter_lag > 30s.
kevin: Also: if you move SLO to metric store, add a noise guardrail: SLO evaluation should fail open if sample coverage < threshold (e.g., < 20% coverage over window). That prevents false alarms caused by low retention.
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Exporter lag alert: otel-collector-us-east exporter_lag=42s reported for 3m.
jess: UX note for console rollouts: show the SLO timeseries and a stacked area for breakdown (queue/network/compute) with a shaded band for retention coverage. On hover show sample_rate and retained_ratio. That makes rollouts less scary when percentiles move because you can see if retention changed.
maria: This is great. I'll do a POC: derive histograms in collector + add retention metric + a dashboard with overlay. Will prototype tail-sampling rule and a sample-weighted metric to compare.
kevin: Happy to help with collector config. I can drop a candidate tail-sampling config later today.
oliver: I'll draft the alert rules for retained_ratio and exporter_lag.
jess: And I'll mock the console overlay in the dashboard kit.
maria: Thanks all :raised_hands: — assigning follow-ups in the doc.
